title: Ragdoll Physics with Joint Constraints and Time Control
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements a ragdoll physics simulation with joint constraints and full time control (play, pause, slow-motion, rewind snapshots). No external physics engine — implement simple Verlet integration manually.

SCENE SETUP:
- Dark gray background (0x1a1a2e). Perspective camera at position (0, 4, 12) looking at origin.
- Ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) at (5, 10, 5).
- A ground plane at y=0, size 20x20, color 0x2d2d44, with grid helper overlay.
- The ragdoll is built from spheres and capsule-like cylinders:
  * Head: sphere radius 0.35, color 0xff6b6b, initial position (0, 6.5, 0)
  * Torso: cylinder height 1.2, radius 0.3, color 0x4ecdc4, initial position (0, 5.5, 0)
  * Left Upper Arm: cylinder height 0.8, radius 0.12, color 0xffe66d, initial position (-0.7, 5.8, 0)
  * Right Upper Arm: same but at (0.7, 5.8, 0)
  * Left Lower Arm: cylinder height 0.7, radius 0.1, color 0xf7fff7, initial position (-1.3, 5.8, 0)
  * Right Lower Arm: same but at (1.3, 5.8, 0)
  * Left Upper Leg: cylinder height 0.9, radius 0.15, color 0xa8e6cf, initial position (-0.3, 4.5, 0)
  * Right Upper Leg: same but at (0.3, 4.5, 0)
  * Left Lower Leg: cylinder height 0.8, radius 0.12, color 0xdcedc1, initial position (-0.3, 3.5, 0)
  * Right Lower Leg: same but at (0.3, 3.5, 0)
- Total: 10 body parts.

PHYSICS (Verlet Integration):
- Each body part has a position and previousPosition for Verlet integration.
- Gravity = -9.81 m/s^2 applied each frame (scaled by dt^2).
- Ground collision: clamp y >= (half-height of each part) so parts rest on ground.
- Joint constraints connect adjacent parts with distance constraints (head-torso, torso-upper arms, upper arm-lower arm, torso-upper legs, upper leg-lower leg). Use 8 constraint-solving iterations per frame.
- Each joint has a max angle limit of 90 degrees (use dot product of segment directions to enforce).
- Damping factor: multiply velocity by 0.98 each frame.
- Energy is tracked: totalEnergy = sum of (0.5 * mass * v^2) + (mass * 9.81 * y) for all parts. Mass = 1.0 for all parts.

TIME CONTROL:
- timeScale variable: controls simulation speed multiplier. Default 1.0.
- Simulation states: 'playing', 'paused', 'rewinding'.
- Snapshot system: every 10 frames, save a snapshot of all positions and previousPositions. Store up to 300 snapshots in a circular buffer.
- Frame counter: increments each simulation step.

USER INTERACTIONS:
- Spacebar: toggle play/pause.
- Key 'S': set timeScale to 0.25 (slow motion). If already 0.25, reset to 1.0.
- Key 'R': enter rewind mode — step backward through snapshots at 2 snapshots per second. Press R again to stop rewinding and resume from that state.
- Key 'F': apply a random force impulse to the torso (random direction, magnitude 3-6 units) — only works when playing.
- Key 'G': toggle gravity between -9.81 and -2.0 (moon gravity).
- Key 'D': drop/reset the ragdoll to initial position and clear velocities.
- Click on any body part (raycasting): highlight it yellow and pin it in place (freeze its position). Click again to unpin. Track pinned parts in an array.

HUD (DOM overlay):
- Top-left panel showing: simState, timeScale (2 decimals), frameCount, totalEnergy (1 decimal), gravity value, number of pinned parts, snapshot count.
- Use a div with id='hud', white text, monospace font, semi-transparent black background.

STATE MANAGEMENT — expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
{
  sceneReady: boolean,
  bodyPartCount: number (should be 10),
  simState: 'playing' | 'paused' | 'rewinding',
  timeScale: number,
  frameCount: number,
  gravity: number,
  totalEnergy: number,
  snapshotCount: number,
  pinnedParts: number (count of currently pinned parts),
  headY: number (head sphere world y position),
  torsoY: number,
  allPartsAboveGround: boolean (all parts y >= 0),
  jointConstraintsSatisfied: boolean (all distance constraints within 5% tolerance),
  bodyPartPositions: [{name, x, y, z}] array of all 10 parts,
  energyHistory: [last 5 totalEnergy values],
  lastForceApplied: {x, y, z, magnitude} or null,
  dampingFactor: number
}

ENSURE:
- No NaN in any position or energy value at any time.
- Animation loop uses requestAnimationFrame.
- Verlet integration is stable with the given parameters.
- The ragdoll should visibly fall under gravity when simulation starts.
- All keyboard controls work as described.
physics_constraints: Verlet integration with gravity (-9.81 or -2.0). Distance constraints between connected body parts solved iteratively (8 iterations). Joint angle limits of 90 degrees. Ground plane collision at y=0. Damping factor 0.98. Energy = sum of kinetic + potential for all parts. No NaN values permitted. Parts must never go below ground.
